meta.tagline: The endless city of palms, golden-hour light and taco trucks

pills: A megacity of a hundred neighborhoods
Ocean, mountain and desert in one day

overview.title: Welcome to Los Angeles
overview.intro: Los Angeles is not one city but a hundred towns strung together with palm trees: Venice's canals, Hollywood's hills, Downtown's art deco towers and K-Town's late-night grills build separate worlds on one map. Light is the star here — the film industry moved for this golden hour and never left. Fame is the shop window, but the city's heart beats in the taco truck queue, on the Griffith trail at sunset, and in the wave hitting the shore. To love LA, stop looking for celebrities; look at the light and the table.

local_word.definition: The hour of golden light before sunset: LA's sacred time zone. Filmmakers settled the city for this light, photographers build their day around it, and everyone on the beach falls quiet when it arrives. When planning in LA, first decide where you'll be for golden hour — everything else arranges itself around it.

rules.title: Never plan LA as one city
rules.description: The morning-Venice, noon-Hollywood, evening-Downtown plan melts in traffic: the distances and 'the 405 factor' are real. Choose one zone a day — a beach day, a hills day, a downtown day — and stay inside it. Those who love LA love it zone by zone.

rules.title: Accept the traffic math
rules.description: From 15:30 to 19:00 the freeway is a waiting room in motion: in those hours, stay in the neighborhood you're in. The metro works better than its reputation (Downtown, Hollywood, Santa Monica lines) — but LA's true public transport is patience and a podcast.

rules.title: Trust the trails and the tacos, not the star sidewalk
rules.description: The Walk of Fame is a five-minute glance; LA's real magic lives on Griffith's paths, in the taco truck queue and on the ocean cliffs. Shift your expectation from showcase to light — that's when the city opens.

tip.label: The LA philosophy
tip.text: There is no goal called 'seeing everything' here; there is 'having a beautiful day': one beach, one trail, one taco, one sunset. Four things a day is enough — the fifth gets lost in traffic. No worries: tomorrow is sunny too.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: LA is a freeway civilization: the car is the base, the metro is a surprising helper, and the beach bike path is the most delightful line.

items.title: Arriving from LAX
items.description: LAX is chaotic but the solution is simple: the ride-app pickup zone (LAX-it) or the FlyAway buses. The center is 30–60 minutes by traffic — if you land between 16:00 and 19:00, pack patience.

items.title: Where the metro works
items.description: The B line links Downtown to Hollywood, the E line Downtown to Santa Monica: on those two corridors the metro beats the car. Ride with a TAP card — on game and concert days rail is the secret superpower.

items.title: The car and freeway language
items.description: In LA the freeways take 'the': the 405, the 101, the 10. Navigation is essential and lane discipline loose. Read parking signs to the last line — the LA parking ticket is the city's hidden tax.

items.title: The beach bike path
items.description: The Strand: 35 kilometers of shoreline cycling from Santa Monica to Redondo. The Venice–Santa Monica stretch is the classic — rent in the morning and pedal beside the ocean. This is LA's best 'freeway'.

items.title: The trail network
items.description: From Griffith Park to Runyon Canyon the city is laced with trails: observatory routes, Hollywood Sign viewpoints and canyon walks. A water bottle and sunscreen are the official equipment of an LA hike.

callout.label: Golden hour tip
callout.text: The day's most important transport decision is this: where will you be at golden hour? Griffith Observatory, the El Matador cliffs or the Venice pier — be in that zone by 16:00 and finish the traffic before the light. Sunset is an appointment in LA; you don't arrive late.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In LA choosing a neighborhood is choosing a vacation: the coast's coolness, the hills' views, Downtown's walkability or the Eastside's cafe rhythm.

local_word.definition: The collective name for Santa Monica, Venice and their surroundings: ocean-breezed, yoga-matted, smoothie-cupped LA. The Eastside is another world — vintage shops, coffee roasters, a younger pulse. Angelenos define themselves by these two sides — the joke that 'a Westsider won't cross town' is only half a joke.

items.name: Santa Monica
items.description: The pier, the beach bike path and walkable streets: LA's most practical seaside base. Linked to Downtown by the E line — the only realistic address for a car-free LA plan.

items.name: Venice
items.description: The canals, Abbot Kinney's boutiques and the boardwalk's chaos: LA's free-spirited corner. Surfer mornings, street-artist evenings — for the character seeker.

items.name: Hollywood and WeHo
items.description: Close to the studios, the comedy clubs and the Sunset Strip: the base for a nightlife-first visit. Brace for tourist noise — the payoff is location and energy.

items.name: Downtown (DTLA)
items.description: Art deco towers, Grand Central Market and museums: LA's most walkable district. The metro junction — a smart base for the car-free traveler and the architecture lover.

items.name: Silver Lake and Los Feliz
items.description: Coffee roasters, record stores and the Griffith trails next door: local LA's cafe rhythm. Hills and reservoir walks at the doorstep — for those seeking life, not showcase.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: LA's weather is a joke with a twist: assumed always sunny, it keeps its own moods — June gray, October heat — and every season works if you know the fine print.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Blossom and Clarity
items.subtitle: Spring · Purple jacarandas, green hills
items.description: Winter rains have greened the hills, and in May the jacarandas paint the streets purple. The air is clear, the trails fresh — LA's most photogenic and most balanced season.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In late May do a jacaranda tour: Del Mar Boulevard and the Eastside streets become purple tunnels. A Griffith trail in the morning plus purple streets in the afternoon — the ideal formula of an LA spring.

items.label: Summer
items.name: From June Gloom to Golden Summer
items.subtitle: Summer · Gray mornings, sunny noons, beach evenings
items.description: June mornings on the coast are gray — the 'June Gloom' legend is real; it burns off by noon. July and August are peak beach season: 24°C at the shore, 35°C in the valley. Two climates in one day — that is the LA summer's tease.

callout.label: Gloom note
callout.text: Don't be surprised by a gray June morning sky at the beach: set the swim for the afternoon and give the morning to a museum or breakfast. The shore can run cool — in LA you dress in layers even for the beach.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Locals' Summer
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warmest sea, clearest sunsets
items.description: September and October are LA's secret peak: the ocean at its warmest, the sky clear, the crowds gone. Santa Ana winds bring spells of dry heat — this is the season locals call the real summer.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In early October take a late afternoon at El Matador: the cliff shadows stretch, the water still invites, and golden hour detonates. The summer crowds have left — the LA coast is at its best in these weeks.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Green Hills and Snow Backdrops
items.subtitle: Winter · Mild days, rain breaks, snowy mountain backdrop
items.description: LA winter means sunny 18°C days: rain visits now and then, the hills turn green, the air gets rinsed. In post-rain clarity the snowy San Gabriels settle behind the skyline — the year's best photographic light.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: The morning after rain, go up to Griffith: snowy mountains, the ocean and the skyline in one frame — LA's rarest view. Winter is also museum and Disney Hall season; a cardigan covers the evenings.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The LA table runs from truck to starred menu, but its heart beats in one place: a tortilla, meat off the fire and a wedge of lime.

local_word.definition: Pork marinated in achiote and cooked on a vertical spit, shawarma-style: the taco filling Mexican masters learned from Lebanese immigrants and perfected. A sliver of pineapple falls from the spit on top — the signature taste of LA taco culture. At the truck, say 'al pastor, with everything': onion, cilantro and salsa included.

items.name: The taco truck ritual
items.description: A truck glowing on a night corner, plate in hand, eaten standing: al pastor, carne asada and lime. In LA the taco is not a meal but the city's shared language — the truck with the queue is always the right truck.

items.name: In-N-Out and animal style
items.description: California's cult burger chain: short menu, long secret menu. Give the password 'animal style' (grilled onions, extra sauce) — and leave as someone in the know, not a tourist.

items.name: K-Town Korean BBQ
items.description: Koreatown's tables burn charcoal late into the night: the banchan army, marinated meats and an insatiable atmosphere. America's best Korean cooking outside Seoul lives here.

items.name: A Grand Central Market crawl
items.description: The Downtown market open since 1917: taco counters to third-wave coffee, pupusas to pastrami. Join the lunch crowd — LA's kitchen summarized under one roof.

items.name: The California brunch
items.description: Avocado toast, açaí bowls and cold brew: it looks like a cliché until you eat it on a sunny terrace. LA brunch is not a meal but a weekend liturgy — be ready to queue.

items.name: Baja-style fish tacos
items.description: Crisp-battered fish, cabbage, crema and lime: Baja California's gift to the LA shore. The undisputed answer to a beach-day lunch — a michelada alongside is for the brave.

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: In LA good food follows the queue, not the fame: the starred room wants a reservation, the taco truck wants patience — both are worth it. Eat in the ethnic neighborhoods (K-Town, Boyle Heights, Thai Town, Little Ethiopia): the city's true food map lives there.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows the Hollywood Sign; these six are LA's cliff-sounding, book-scented hidden face.

items.name: El Matador Beach
items.description: Malibu's rocky cove: you descend a cliff stairway to giant rocks and cave arches that turn to silhouettes at sunset. LA's most cinematic beach — at golden hour, be nowhere else.

items.rarity: A free palace on the hill
items.name: The Getty Center
items.description: The white marble art complex reached by tram: the collection free, the gardens sculptural, the view running to the ocean. Give it half a day — LA's most gracious gift.

items.name: The Bradbury Building and the Last Bookstore
items.description: The wrought-iron light atrium of 1893 (familiar from Blade Runner) and, two blocks away, the book tunnels of the Last Bookstore: DTLA's most photogenic pair. They fit one afternoon.

items.name: The Venice Canals
items.description: Two streets in from the boardwalk chaos, canals from 1905: ducks, wooden bridges and gardened houses. Walk them at sunset — the dream Venice was named for still stands here.

items.name: Griffith's back trails
items.description: Tourists face the Hollywood Sign from the front; you walk Griffith Park's back trails (the Charlie Turner or Wonder View routes) — sign, observatory and city in one frame, half the crowd.

items.rarity: An art picnic on the hill
items.name: Barnsdall Art Park
items.description: The hilltop park around Frank Lloyd Wright's Hollyhock House: sunset picnics under olive trees, summer wine evenings. Los Feliz's local secret — the calmest lawn with a Hollywood view.

callout.label: Light strategy
callout.text: LA's hidden corners run on light: the Getty at noon, the canals in the late afternoon, El Matador at golden hour, the observatory at night. The same place is ordinary in the wrong light and unforgettable in the right one — in this city, the hour outranks the address.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: LA's traps wait in fame's shadow; know these four and live the city by its light, not its shop window.

items.name: Walk of Fame expectations
items.description: The starred sidewalk is crowded, loud and plainer than imagined; the costumed characters charge after the photo.
items.instead: Look for five minutes, take the picture, move on — and know the costume photo costs money before you pose. Live the real Hollywood on a studio tour (Warner Bros) or at a movie in El Capitan.

items.name: Celebrity-home tour vans
items.description: 'Celebrity homes' tours are mostly an expensive traffic experience past tall hedges and guessed addresses.
items.instead: Spend that money on the Warner Bros studio tour or the Getty: cinema itself is more interesting than a celebrity's hedge. For neighborhood curiosity, gliding through Beverly Hills in your own car is free.

items.name: Ignoring the traffic math
items.description: 'Venice to Hollywood, 25 minutes' says the map; at 17:00 the truth is 80. The visitor who plans across town sees LA through a windshield.
items.instead: Hold to the one-zone-a-day rule; make crossings between 10:00 and 15:00. Build the evening where you already are — meeting golden hour on a freeway is LA's most classic regret.

items.name: Not reading the parking sign
items.description: LA parking signs are layered legal documents: misreading costs a ticket or a tow, and beach lots multiply prices on event days.
items.instead: Read EVERY line of the sign; when unsure, use an app-listed garage. On beach days go early or walk a few blocks from a neighborhood street — a ticketless day is a won day in LA.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In LA the best things are either free or queued: the beach, the trail and golden hour cost nothing; the taco and the brunch cost a queue. Pay for light and food, not fame — the city will show you more than stars.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From beach morning to observatory night

steps.title: Venice morning
steps.description: Watch the surfers while the boardwalk wakes, then turn into the canals: Venice's two faces in morning calm.

steps.title: The beach bike ride
steps.description: Pedal the Strand to Santa Monica: ocean on your left, palms on your right. The Ferris wheel photo at the pier is the classic.

steps.title: Fish taco lunch
steps.description: Baja-style crisp fish tacos with lime and cabbage: the beach day's undisputed lunch.

steps.title: DTLA hours
steps.description: Cross to Downtown on the E line: the Bradbury's light atrium, the Last Bookstore tunnels and a Grand Central Market coffee.

steps.title: Griffith golden hour
steps.description: Reach the observatory before sunset: the city turns orange with the Hollywood Sign alongside. This is LA's appointed hour.

steps.title: Taco truck night
steps.description: Stop at the glowing truck on the way home: al pastor 'with everything'. Standing, plate in hand — an LA day closes this way.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Coast, hills and a hundred neighborhoods — the full LA

steps.title: Classic LA
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Venice, the Strand, fish tacos, DTLA, Griffith golden hour, a taco truck.

steps.title: Malibu and Getty day
steps.description: Art and gardens at the Getty in the morning; the PCH drive up Malibu at noon; swimming and cave-hunting at El Matador in the afternoon; golden hour on the sand and a seafood dinner in a beach town.

steps.title: Hills and the Eastside
steps.description: Runyon or a Griffith back trail in the morning; a Los Feliz–Silver Lake coffee-and-records crawl at noon; the Wright house on Barnsdall's hill in the afternoon; a farewell K-Town Korean BBQ night — a long close at a charcoal table.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: LA English is relaxed, sunny and freeway-accented; these five phrases tune you to the city's frequency.

items.meaning: Freeways take 'the' — 'the 405 was brutal' is the universal LA opener
The gray coastal cloud of June mornings — burns off by noon; locals don't blink
The major-traffic-jam alert — reroute when you hear it on the radio
Address, exclamation, punctuation — the all-purpose salt of LA sentences
It's all fine — the official seal of California ease; use liberally
